decision: Bump next and eslint-config-next from 16.3.4 to 16.4.1 (lockfile resolves @next/env, @next/eslint-plugin-next 16.4.1 and sharp 0.35.5) to clear CRITICAL GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw, GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr and GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j
rationale: 16.4.1 is the lowest release on the 16.x line patched for all three advisories (GHSA-vcvr is fixed from 16.3.6; the other two from 16.4.1). The Image Optimization API (/_next/image) is enabled with default config, is not covered by middleware.ts (matcher /api/:path*), runs on glibc (node:22-bookworm-slim) and the deployed images ship sharp 0.35.4 (< 0.35.5 per the advisory workaround). A security fix overrides the repo's >=2-week-old pin convention.
alternatives: 16.3.6-16.3.8 rejected: still vulnerable to GHSA-2464 and GHSA-673q (fixed only in 16.4.1). 16.4.2-16.4.6 rejected: newer than needed for the fix, more unreviewed change. Overriding sharp alone to >=0.35.5 rejected: leaves GHSA-673q unpatched and the Trivy gate red.

decision: Scope the PR to the CRITICAL next advisories only; the remaining fixable HIGH findings (brace-expansion, dompurify, @grpc/grpc-js, js-yaml, nanoid, postcss, protobufjs, smol-toml, source-map-js, ws) stay for a separate PR
rationale: The CI Trivy fs gate blocks only on fixable CRITICAL; HIGH is report-only. Local Trivy 0.70.0 (the version trivy-action v0.36.0 installs) shows 0 CRITICAL after the bump and no other CRITICAL in bun.lock. The bump also clears two HIGH next findings (CVE-2026-94482, CVE-2026-94483).
alternatives: Bumping the HIGH set here rejected: mixes unrelated dependency churn into an urgent security fix and widens the review surface.
